simulator.policy: One method-neutral environment and identical outcome criteria for every condition. Never grade a preferred choreography or pool results across changed task/environment versions.
changes: Record actual completed tool occurrences and necessary input causality, without imposing one total invocation order.
Model actual 4M repository source bytes, published bytes and content-bound review/test results.
Bind publication to completed exact-content review/test receipts at the time of the effect; later validation cannot authorize an earlier publication.
14E analysis receipts bind actual prepared cells, compound versions and completed inputs. submit_decision records an actual decision, and documentation requires that completed decision.

13E preparation, compound and assay results name their actual completed input occurrences. Molecular and separation quality results may complete in either order, but must cover the same assay and current compound before final validation.

13M QC approvals bind completed measurements and the actual purified specimen or biological trial. Rejection requires a fresh measurement/trial before re-verification; a new chemist measurement does not invent a new batch. Independent QC/quality order and instrument-free bioassay overlap remain legal. Synthesis names and optional culture strings remain actual caller data.
Accept independent legal schedules and recoverable failed attempts. Retain already-observed unsafe publication and physical conflicts rather than erasing them after recovery.

Version 3 medical worlds bind completed patient results and current own-panel test or imaging inputs. Public test_type is preserved, including partial panels; independent general/cardiac panels, imaging and caller-data medication review stay independent. No diagnosis-before-review gate or unobservable prescribing/administration claim is introduced.

Version 5 code-development tools bind implementation, test definitions, review, merge, CI and staging to actual source/repository hashes and completed receipts. Merge and deployment effects remain observable when unsafe; later evidence cannot authorize them retroactively. CI validates the existing integrated base before another merge, and staging records current validated service dependencies. Review and test preparation can reorder independently. These are abstract tool outcomes, not execution of an actual code compiler.

Version 7 allows repair of the latest failed publication after a completed negative CI with exact publication and test inputs, using a fresh implementation and its completed matching review. Draft preparation and review may overlap the pending CI. Unrelated, stale, pending or input-invalid failures do not justify a repair. Unsafe merge effects still execute and retain violations. Returned argument and result snapshots cannot mutate past evidence.

Version 8 replaces 7E's done-bit world with actual document/reference versions, completed review inputs and captured combination receipts. Both writers may revise either chapter. All 720 preparation/review permutations are checked, with 48 valid schedules; no fixed writer or reference-update order is imposed. Pending results cannot authorize a combination. Unsafe combinations remain observable and later repairs do not erase their violations.

Version 9 unifies 7E/7M/7H actual document, figure, fact and editorial data in one journal-based model. Created figures must exist and match insertion inputs; completed content-bound evidence is required at publication. Independent preparation and part reviews remain free.

Version 10 adds a method-neutral read_section tool to 7M. It returns the actual completed chapter and version ID, never in-flight content, and keeps reads independent of the other chapters' preparation. No workflow or required writer order is added. Using the returned content in actual 7M coordination/effects and the full 7H minor-edit contract remain unqualified.
Version 11 adds actual reagent and compound inputs, cascading content-bound QC and independent physical instruments for 13H. The common data model is qualified, not its application port.

Version 12 replaces build done maps and first-call counters with actual material contents, unique completed object occurrences, matching test/validation receipts and actual link inputs. Either 10E builder may start; B can build against provided types and rebuild after A changes them. All initial build permutations and both test/validation orders remain available. Unsafe linking remains a recorded effect; later checks cannot repair an old link. Physical resource use follows the actual requested module, with two build slots and independent workers in 10H. These remain synthetic compiler/data outcomes, not execution of a real compiler.

Version 14 kitchen 12E/12M bind assigned dishes, ingredients and recipients to completed material occurrences. 12H cooking names its actual completed preparation; failure consumes that preparation, and a fresh completed preparation allows recovery. Plating binds completed successful cooking and the correct completed ingredient. Returned replies cannot mutate the world journal. Completion waits for the final effect reply. Independent orders and different-equipment overlaps remain free; conflicts are observed without scheduling or locks. Kitchen progress is derived from the effect journal; the old acquire/release methods and prep/cooked/done tables are removed.

Version 15 unifies 14E/14M material receipts, failed/pending replacement handling and actual decisions. 14M regulatory review binds the completed current decision, rejection requires a new decision without prescribing extra assays, and documentation requires its current approval. Shared journals own copied input/result data. Independent calls remain unscheduled; resource conflicts stay visible. The 14M application and 14H world/port are not qualified by these tests.

Version 16 replaces 14H done maps and its ignored sample counter with actual compound/formulation, positive or negative assay outcomes, clinical assessment, regulatory evidence and a recorded director outcome. Three total samples are consumed once by valid bio/tox attempts including failures; culture preparation and invalid inputs consume none. Retry does not replenish stock. An exhausted/failed study may support an honest abort, never positive continuation. A hold on unchanged evidence needs deeper dual-instrument review or new scientific evidence. The simulator neither schedules callers nor consults Hibana/EPF. Independent assay orders remain free. Director decision is exposed equally to all methods; the phantom duplicate clinical mass-spec requirement is removed. Synthetic 1–5 second instrument/review delays are common to all methods. Prior source-bound results retain their older worlds.

Version 17 gives every scientific result a run-local event_id, including injected failures, exhaustion and clinical holds. A positive artifact_id remains absent on failure. Clinical inputs can therefore cite the exact negative occurrence without inventing a successful artifact or a new sample. The ID is derived from the existing owned event journal; no workflow flag, owner table or additional counter is introduced. The same response field is available to every method. Earlier v15/v16 source-bound qualifications remain distinct.

Version 18 gives 3M actual completed research artifacts, section/reference material, fact and editorial receipts, and publication-time evidence through the shared document journal. Extra research topics remain free; each assigned section still needs its own actual inputs. Each completed section can be checked and edited before other authors start. Resource requirements come only from existing common metadata, including DATABASE exclusion. Neither a choreography nor caller scheduling is introduced. Earlier source-bound results retain their recorded worlds.
